findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Resolve the write-fence for every supported `sync.remote` backend — including the S3/git-remote-s3 backend (ADR 0093) which has no pre-receive hook — or explicitly scope S3 out of the reclamation with a stated fallback, so the fence + portability claim hold for all remotes.
evidence: Plan: 'The fence is a SERVER-SIDE ref-lock / pre-receive hold on the remote's tickets ref for the brief swap window'
Plan: 'Mechanism (portable, out-of-band; NO CI-provider dependence)'

docs/adr/0093-s3-ticket-store-backend.md (Accepted 2026-08-20): `sync.remote` may be an `s3://` bucket via git-remote-s3, which stores branches as git bundles under a key prefix — there is no git server / pre-receive hook; concurrency is handled by a bundle-per-push auto-doctor (`src/rebar/_store/s3_doctor.py`), not ref locks
config-reference.md: `sync.remote` default 'origin' but configurable; test_sync_remote_config.py exercises 'gerrit' and s3 rehearsal remotes
findings.finding: The write-fence feasibility resolution assumes a server-side pre-receive/ref-lock hold on the remote's `tickets` ref, but the S3 backend (ADR 0093, an accepted `sync.remote` target) has no git server and no pre-receive hook — so the fence is unrealizable there and the portability/no-CI-provider-dependence claim breaks.
findings.location: Feasibility section — 'The write-fence needs NO clone registry (G6)'; DESIGN+PROOF comment; AC 'Remote-side write-fence feasibility resolved without a clone registry'
scenarios: A deployment running the S3 ticket-store backend attempts the reclamation swap; the plan's fence cannot be applied, so in-flight/unpushed writes during the swap window are lost beyond the accepted >N-day case
The S0 ADR claims portability but the fence only exists for a subset of remotes
findings.suggested_fix: For the S3 backend, define the fence in terms of git-remote-s3's per-ref push lock (s3_doctor `acquire_lock`/`release_lock`) plus bundle-quiesce, or restrict reclamation to git-hosted remotes and document that S3 stores are excluded until a bundle-level fence is designed.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the concrete server-side fence primitive per remote type (and stop citing ADR 0031's client-side CAS / ADR 0011's GitHub-only ruleset as if they were a portable pre-receive hold), so the atomic swap-window guarantee is grounded in an actually-available mechanism.
evidence: docs/adr/0031-reconciler-ref-lock.md: the lock is a CLIENT-driven `git hash-object -w` + `git update-ref <ref> <oid> <old>` create-only CAS on a bare ref (`refs/reconciler/lock`), explicitly 'not a full fencing token' with 'no stale-writer rejection … of the protected resource'

docs/adr/0011-github-mirror-lock.md + infra/github/apply-mirror-lock.sh: mirror-lock is a GitHub repo-level ruleset (`gerrit-mirror-lock-main`) — a GitHub-provider construct, not a portable pre-receive hook
Plan claims these back a 'SERVER-SIDE ref-lock / pre-receive hold'
findings.finding: The named precedents for the server-side fence (ADR 0031 reconciler-ref-lock, ADR 0011 mirror-lock) do not actually establish a server-side pre-receive hold: ADR 0031 is a client-side bare-ref CAS via `git update-ref`, and ADR 0011 is a GitHub-specific repo ruleset — neither is a portable server-side pre-receive fence on the tickets ref.
findings.location: Feasibility section — 'precedent: ADR 0031 reconciler-ref-lock, ADR 0011 mirror-lock'
scenarios: The S0 ADR proof cites 0031/0011 as sufficient precedent, but a reviewer/implementer finds the primitives are client-side CAS and a provider ruleset, so the actual server-side fence mechanism is still unspecified for a generic remote

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a child slice implementing S2 history coalescing (fast-import/commit-tree baseline synthesis, authorship_ledger carry, enforce_since re-anchor) on a disposable shadow clone with fsck/replay/verify-authorship and a two-clone resurrection test.
evidence: Parent: 'S2 coalescing prototyped on a DISPOSABLE SHADOW CLONE (never pushed); fsck/replay/verify-authorship clean on that shadow branch; two-clone resurrection test.'

Parent: '.retired files are blobs; the guarded pack is blobless => .retired GC alone shrinks it by ~0. The real lever is collapsing per-event history into SNAPSHOT-anchored checkpoints below the horizon.'
Parent S2: 'Broadened from .retired-only to commit/tree reclamation (the object-count lever).'
51a7 description: 'removes eligible .retired tombstones + folded companions' — no commit/tree coalescing, no shadow-clone prototype, no fast-import baseline synthesis, no two-clone resurrection test.
container pairing: parent + 51a7-5d9b-95cb-4903/866f-440c-3686-42df/aff9-1252-ad21-4695/e32d-6ea1-029a-435d
findings.finding: No child covers the parent's core S2 deliverable: history coalescing / commit-tree reclamation on a disposable shadow clone. The parent's entire quantified win depends on 'collapsing per-event history into SNAPSHOT-anchored checkpoints' (commit/tree reclamation), yet the only sweep child (51a7) is scoped to '.retired tombstones + folded companions' — the very blob-removal the parent proves yields ~0 pack shrink.
findings.location: child 51a7-5d9b-95cb-4903 (and roster gap: no S2 coalescing sibling)
scenarios: Completion verifier checks the parent deferred item 'S2 coalescing prototyped on a disposable shadow clone; two-clone resurrection test' and finds no child delivering it; the epic's stated pack-shrink goal is unachievable via the enumerated children.
findings.suggested_fix: Create an S2 child owning commit/tree coalescing to a re-signed baseline checkpoint on a never-pushed shadow clone; keep 51a7 as the downstream .retired sidecar reclaim that rides on it (as 51a7 itself notes).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile 51a7 scope with the parent: reframe it as the sidecar/blob reclaim that rides on the S2 commit/tree coalescing, not as the primary pack-shrink sweep.
evidence: 51a7 title/description: 'Branch-wide GC sweep of eligible .retired events (portable)' ... 'The actual sweep that removes eligible .retired tombstones + folded companions.'
Parent 'Quantified win — insufficient alone': '.retired GC alone shrinks it by ~0. The real lever is collapsing per-event history...'
Parent S2: reclamation 'Broadened from .retired-only to commit/tree reclamation (the object-count lever).'
container pairing: parent + 51a7-5d9b-95cb-4903/866f-440c-3686-42df/aff9-1252-ad21-4695/e32d-6ea1-029a-435d
findings.finding: Child 51a7's scope contradicts the parent's own quantified finding: it plans a '.retired GC sweep' as 'the actual sweep,' but the parent establishes that .retired GC alone shrinks the blobless pack by ~0 and that the object-count lever is commit/tree reclamation. This is a conflicting-assumption / scope-narrowing inconsistency between child and parent.
scenarios: 51a7 completes 'the actual sweep' of .retired files, the pack does not shrink, and the health-lane bug remains unblocked despite the child being marked done.
findings.suggested_fix: Re-scope 51a7 to explicitly depend on the (missing) S2 coalescing child and state that its pack contribution is the blob sidecar reclaim, not the object-count lever.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Assign an S2 child ownership of the fast-import/commit-tree baseline emission plus the backup-ref + shadow-branch staged, revertible swap and rollback verification.
evidence: Parent AC: 'History-rewrite primitive named as core-git and its portability resolved.' and 'Risk assessment plus rollback (backup ref, shadow-branch stage) designed.'
Parent S2/Risk: 'Reclamation emits the new history with git fast-import ...'; 'Rollback: immutable backup ref refs/tickets-backup/pre-reclaim-<date> ... the swap is one revertible ref update.'
No child description mentions fast-import, commit-tree, the backup ref, or the staged swap; 51a7 says only 'removes eligible .retired tombstones.'
container pairing: parent + 51a7-5d9b-95cb-4903/866f-440c-3686-42df/aff9-1252-ad21-4695/e32d-6ea1-029a-435d
findings.finding: Owned-by-none scope gap: the parent's history-rewrite primitive (S2 'the rewrite primitive is core-git ... git fast-import ... preflight asserts git fast-import --version') and the risk/rollback machinery (backup ref refs/tickets-backup/pre-reclaim-<date>, shadow-branch stage, revertible swap) are not owned by any child. 51a7 performs removal but does not name fast-import/commit-tree emission, the backup ref, or the shadow-branch staged swap.
scenarios: Approved rollout proceeds but no child implemented the backup-ref/shadow-branch swap or the fast-import baseline emission; the destructive step has no owning slice with rollback wiring.
findings.suggested_fix: Fold the fast-import primitive + backup-ref/shadow-branch swap into the new S2 coalescing child; have 51a7 and aff9 depend on it.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Author explicit acceptance criteria on each child (866f/e32d/aff9/51a7) so parent-criterion coverage can be confirmed rather than inferred from descriptions.
evidence: show_ticket for all four children returns no acceptance-criteria field; only 'description'.
Pass rule: 'A sibling whose roster block shows only its - <id>: <title> line has no parseable criteria ... treat that sibling as indeterminate for the absence test.'
container pairing: parent + 51a7-5d9b-95cb-4903/866f-440c-3686-42df/aff9-1252-ad21-4695/e32d-6ea1-029a-435d
findings.finding: Coverage is indeterminate for the absence test: none of the four children carry parseable acceptance criteria (their tickets and the roster expose only title+description). Coverage judgments above rest on descriptions alone, which the pass rules classify as indeterminate rather than confirmed coverage.
scenarios: A parent criterion appears covered by a child's title/description but the child's eventual AC narrow the outcome, silently leaving the parent criterion uncovered.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the event-file-replay path with the store's existing MERGE-as-union non-FF recovery (`push_recovery._recover_non_fast_forward`): specify how a live <N-day clone's automatic push-recovery is redirected to replay-onto-baseline instead of union-merging a no-common-ancestor tip.
evidence: docs/concurrency.md:531-551: 'both reconverge by MERGE-as-union, never rebase'; on non-FF, `push_tickets_branch` → `_recover_non_fast_forward` 'fetches and merges the remote tickets branch as a union before a bounded retry'

The plan's replay requires a manual reset+re-stage step, but a normal clone hitting the rewritten tip will instead auto-invoke the union-merge recovery (no common ancestor → merge failure or unbounded divergence)
findings.finding: The unpushed-write reconciliation is specified as EVENT-FILE REPLAY ('reset tracking ref to baseline, re-stage local-only event files, commit — not a history merge'), but the live store's non-fast-forward recovery path is MERGE-as-union (`push_recovery._recover_non_fast_forward`); the plan does not reconcile how a rewritten, no-common-ancestor baseline interacts with that automatic union-merge recovery that every clone runs on the next push.
findings.location: Feasibility section — '<N-day clone's UNPUSHED events reconcile by EVENT-FILE REPLAY … not a history merge, so the absent common ancestor is irrelevant'
scenarios: A live <N-day clone with unpushed writes simply performs its next auto-write/auto-push after the swap; it hits the existing non-FF union-merge recovery against a no-common-ancestor tip rather than the plan's hand-run event-file replay, and either fails to converge or resurrects pre-baseline history

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify and prove the post-rollback state across ALL clone states — including clones that already force-reset to the rewritten baseline and replayed unpushed events during the window — so that reverting the remote ref restores a consistent, correctly-interpreted store (attach a literal DATA LOSS RISK note for any clone state where reconciliation cannot recover replayed unpushed events).
evidence: 'the swap is one revertible ref update' — asserts rollback completes, not post-rollback cross-clone state
S3 forces stale/reconnecting clones to reset to the new baseline; a subsequent remote-ref revert does not un-reset those clones
'<N-day clone's UNPUSHED events reconcile by EVENT-FILE REPLAY onto the new baseline' — replay targets the rewritten baseline, which a rollback abandons
T11 post-rollback overlay applies: plan rewrites persisted records in place / one-way transformation, not purely additive
findings.finding: The rollback design asserts the swap is 'one revertible ref update' but never asserts on the persisted STATE after rollback across clones that already force-reset to the rewritten baseline during the swap window; reverting the remote ref returns the remote tip while leaving those clones pointing at (and having replayed unpushed event files onto) the now-abandoned rewritten baseline.
scenarios: Swap completes; some clones reconnect and force-reset to the rewritten baseline; a defect is found and the remote ref is reverted to the backup — those clones now diverge from the restored history and their replayed unpushed events sit on an orphaned baseline
findings.suggested_fix: Add a rollback AC that the backup-ref revert is paired with a defined clone-side re-reconciliation (re-detect drift, reset to the restored backup tip, re-replay any unpushed event files onto the restored baseline), and prove no ACKed-or-replayed write is stranded on the abandoned rewritten baseline.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify that S1-S3 reclamation is resumable/idempotent: define the recovery/abort path for a failed offline rewrite and for a swap that aborts after fencing (fence release, backup-ref reuse, safe re-run) so a partially-completed migration leaves the store on a known-good tip.
evidence: The plan describes the rewrite (fast-import baseline synthesis) and a single swap, but no step covers partial-failure recovery of the rewrite or an aborted swap
ABSENCE: no statement that S1-S3 are idempotent / re-runnable, e.g. that re-issuing reclamation against an already-rewritten or partially-fenced remote is safe
T11 checklist: 'A partially-completed migration is resumable/idempotent'
findings.finding: Migration resumability/idempotency of the offline rewrite and the cutover is not specified: the plan does not state what happens if the offline fast-import rewrite fails partway or if the swap aborts after the ref-fence is taken but before the ref update completes, nor whether the reclamation is re-runnable without double-applying.
scenarios: fast-import crashes mid-synthesis in the disposable clone
ref-fence acquired and backup ref written, but the ref-swap fails or the operator aborts — is the fence released and the store left on the original tip?

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] When filing W1, cite existing prior art ADR 0039 (write-time batched commits / batch_stage_and_commit) and frame W1 as extending its import-only batch carve-out to the enrichment/digest lane rather than a net-new batch design, addressing ADR 0039's durability rationale for the enrichment/digest events.
evidence: ADR 0039: 'batch_stage_and_commit ... collapsing N events into a single commit ... sets the long-term growth rate of the tickets branch'; batching is currently 'import-only; interactive writes are never batched'
Plan describes W1 as a fresh 'structural fix ... out of scope, discovered_from this epic' with no reference to the existing batch primitive
findings.finding: W1 ('batch the enrichment/digest write lane') is presented as a novel out-of-scope structural follow-up without noting existing prior art ADR 0039, which already implemented a write-time batched-commit primitive (`batch_stage_and_commit`) explicitly to reduce the tickets-branch growth rate — risking repackaging rather than extending existing machinery.
findings.location: Quantified win (W1 'batch the enrichment/digest write lane'); Deferred 'W1/W2 filed'
scenarios: W1 is filed as a new epic that re-derives a batch-commit design already shipped in ADR 0039 rather than extending its import-only carve-out to the enrichment/digest lane

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the new remote-anchored N-day horizon and the event-file-replay-onto-baseline scheme with existing prior art ADR 0035 (snapshot-horizon-safe-replay / COMPACTION_HORIZON_NS), and prove the replayed event files sort after the baseline commit so the RC2-class positional-skip drop cannot recur.
evidence: ADR 0035 §'Option 3 — conservative fold horizon': 'Compaction folds an event only once it is older than compact.COMPACTION_HORIZON_NS ... the live events sort after the snapshot and replay on top of compiled_state instead of being positionally skipped'

Plan proposes a distinct 'remote-anchored horizon' (N=30d) and asserts unpushed events 'reconcile by EVENT-FILE REPLAY onto the new baseline ... re-stage the local-only append-only event files, commit' — conceptually adjacent to ADR 0035's replay-ordering guarantees but not cross-referenced
The plan cites ADR 0031 and ADR 0011 for the write-fence but no horizon/replay ADR for its core horizon+replay mechanism
findings.finding: The plan invents a new remote-anchored N-day horizon + event-file-replay-onto-baseline scheme without reconciling against existing in-repo prior art ADR 0035 (snapshot-horizon-safe-replay), which already establishes a conservative fold HORIZON (COMPACTION_HORIZON_NS) and 'replay on top of the snapshot' ordering semantics for concurrent clones.
findings.location: Design + proof (C1–C5); Feasibility ("reconcile by EVENT-FILE REPLAY onto the new baseline")
scenarios: S1 eligibility / S2 coalescing interacts with the existing COMPACTION_HORIZON_NS hot-edge horizon, producing two independently-defined horizons with possibly conflicting replay-ordering assumptions
A <N-day clone's replayed event files must sort AFTER the new baseline commit to avoid the RC2-class positional-skip drop ADR 0035 fixed
findings.suggested_fix: In the DESIGN + PROOF comment, add a prior-art subsection citing ADR 0035; state how the two horizons compose and show the baseline commit is gap-timestamped so replayed <N-day events sort after it (as ADR 0035 requires) rather than being positionally skipped.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Justify the choice of git fast-import/mktree for S2 coalescing against the established core-git `git replace --graft` (grafts/replacement refs) alternative, stating why full re-emission is preferred over (or staged before) a graft-based collapse.
evidence: Plan: 'Reclamation emits the new history with git fast-import (equivalently git mktree/git commit-tree plumbing) ... so the disposable clone needs no git filter-repo'
git-scm docs (retrieved): `git replace --graft` is a core-git primitive for re-parenting/collapsing history; filter-repo itself uses `git replace --graft` under the hood
The plan resolves fast-import vs third-party filter-repo, but does not weigh fast-import vs the core-git graft/replace approach
findings.finding: The S2 coalescing names git fast-import / git mktree / git commit-tree as THE rewrite primitive but does not consider the established core-git history-collapse alternative `git replace --graft` (grafts / replacement refs), so the primitive choice is not justified against an equally-core, arguably lower-risk established approach.
findings.location: Feasibility, 'The rewrite primitive is core-git, not third-party (T3)'; Deferred S2
scenarios: Choosing full fast-import re-emission rewrites every SHA (accepted, but maximal blast radius); a graft/replace-based collapse may achieve the object-count reduction with a narrower rewrite or serve as a lower-risk staging step
